scope: Proposition 7 of the manuscript “Snaky in 21 Maker moves” (preprints/Snaky-in-21-Maker-moves-September-25-2026/article.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 187 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e5ce107fdc4ec77f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose it is Maker’s turn at an arbitrary finite position, Maker owns the four cells {(0, 0), (1, 0), (2, 0), (3, 0)}, and Breaker owns at most three cells in Q = ([−3, 6] × [−4, 4]) ∩ Z2 . Then Maker has already won or can force a win. Additional Maker cells and arbitrary Breaker cells outside Q are allowed.
